474.t: Five years with Isaiah Morgan and his drummers
474.s: Morgan's drummers (Albert Giles and others), Morgan's nickname Ike, and Johnson Ridge.
474.ch: New Orleans bands: Cheek, Parker, Morgan
474.q: Yeah, I said we had Cleo, I forgot Cleo was writing then. Albert Giles or either Lionel Tarraganda or either Nolan Williams. Or that's another drummer you never heard of him.

259.t: Bobby the drummer, Black Benny and the break-up of Vincent's band
259.s: Vincent says drummer Bobby played with Chris Kelly and then with his band, followed by Black Benny. After Maurice Durant returned from the war and tried to boss the band, it broke up, and he recalls the players joking about age.
259.q: What band was that? Let me see my band. Oh, that was a little bit of a band. Bobby used to play. And we had facial for it. And with facial and that, we got Bobby. And when Bobby left, we got Black Benny. And that's where Black Benny said he was going to make a man out of himself. And Black Benny…

40.t: Drummer change: JJ Joyce replaces Bob McIntyre
40.s: JJ Joyce, a dental student with a parade-style snare and bass drum approach, replaced Bob McIntyre; otherwise the band is unchanged.
40.q: Well, the original drummer with the group was Bob McIntyre. And, well, a couple months back, Bob's wife had a baby. And, naturally, Bob had to give more time to his family, you know, and he couldn't get out the way he wanted to make these jobs at night. And, then, John Joyce, JJ started playing…

681.s: Hirsch wanted Whiteman's drum chair but Whiteman would not take him from his friend Himber, and George Wettling got it.
681.ch: California, New York and Richard Himber
681.q: He was the last of the fixers of us. So about that time, the one thing that I wanted more than anything in the world was to go with Whiteman's band. On drums. And the old man was just about ready but just before he hired George Wettling, he was talking to me. And then he found out that I was...…

195.t: Leaving the Doughboys, Mineral Wells transcriptions, and no drums
195.s: He left the Doughboys full time around 1939-40 for school but kept playing afternoons and records. The bands still used no drums, only an occasional clarinet or trombone.
195.q: any idea about that that's after i left when did you leave the doughboys oh it must have been about 39 or 40 or 70 here the story is i left the doughboys and continued to play on with them in other groups i couldn't play their noon program because i was going to school but we'd play afternoon…

573.t: Replacing Roy Evans: the band's drummers
573.s: Names the drummers used over the years, including Alfred Williams.
573.q: Well, I think we're taking Alfred Williams, Sam's old drummer. He's still living here. He's here now. Yes, I know. Well, he played with me. He used to make all the trips with me. We didn't have no drummer. Well, Sean was the first drummer that we had. Then after Sean left, we'd taken Roy. Sean used…

128.t: Sequence of drummers: Rudolph, Sean and Roy
128.s: How Rudolph, Sean and then Roy took the drum chair and why Sam let drummers go.
128.q: Oh well you know, Mr. Misunderstood him and Sam you know. That's why Sam got rid of me and got another drum player. Sam got rid of me and got Roy. Roy played drums.

135.t: Connie Kay's stroke, Mickey Roker, then Tootie Heath replaces him
135.s: Heath recalls Connie's stroke before a Hogwood Brandenburg concert in Boston, Mickey Roker joining, then Tootie taking the drum chair until Milt died.
135.q: Mickey, because when Connie died, Milt, who had been playing with Mickey on his jobs, said, “I asked Mickey, and Mickey said he’d be honored to play with us,” so when he did that without any vote from John…

235.t: Changing drummers at the Paradise: Timmie Kennedy to Kalil
235.s: He replaced Tim Kennedy with Kalil for more experience against visiting stars, and sometimes used Art Blakey, Kenny Clarke or Max Roach.
235.ch: The Paradise and life in Queens
235.q: : At the Paradise, yeah, he stayed with me a long time. I saw Timmie the other night at the Village Vanguard and I...you see I had to change drummers because, you know, all these guys, Gene Ammons, and Bird, and all these guys would come up there and Art Blakey and Max Roach and all these guys, so…

124.t: Bill Beeson takes Chick's drum chair
124.s: The band returns to the Savoy briefly; senior men run it, with Chick's friend Bill Beeson on drums, though no one could fill Chick's place.
124.ch: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
124.q: And then we, you know, come back to the Savoy Ballroom. No, I think it was about a week later (inaudible) went back to the ballroom -- the Savoy Ballroom for a couple of (inaudible) days, you know.
